name: first_hour_range_breakout_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: The first hour (09:15-10:15) establishes a range that captures initial order flow, position adjustments, and reaction to overnight news. Breakouts from this range after 10:15 signal genuine directional commitment that persists into the afternoon. Unlike 15-min ORB, the 1-hour range is more stable and produces fewer false breakouts. The inefficiency exists because many participants who set up in the first hour have stops just outside the range — triggering a cascade on breakout. Not fully arbitraged because the wait (1 hour) tests patience.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters and closes inside range for 5 bars

weaknesses: Low frequency: 0-1 trades per day. Many days have no breakout, or breakout happens too late for meaningful P&L.
On days when the first hour range is very tight (<0.3%), any breakout is likely noise and the target is too small to cover costs.
Afternoon reversals can erase morning breakout profits — the market has a tendency to mean-revert in the last 90 minutes.
prior_art: First hour range breakout. Variant of ORB with longer initial range. See: Toby Crabel, Mark Fisher.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
